prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Late in the cold night wakened, and heard wind, And lay with eyes closed and silent, knowing These words how bodiless they are, this darkness Empty under my roof and the panes rattling Roughed by wind. And so lay and imagined Somewhere far off black seas heavy-shouldered Plunging on sand and the ebb off-streaming and Thunder forever. So lying bethought me, friend, What traffic ghouls have, or this be legend, In low inland hollows of the earth, under Shade of moon, the night moaning, and bitter frost; And feared the riches of my bones, long given Into this earth, should tumble to their hands. No girl or ghost beside me, and I lonely, Remembering gardens, lilac scent, or twilight Descending late in summer on that town, I lay and found my years departed from me, And feared the cold bed and the wind, absurdly Alone with silence and the trick of tears.

Please expand the following bullet points into a complete, well-structured text:

* The speaker wakes up alone on a cold, windy night in a dark house filled with rattling windowpanes.
* Lying in the dark, the speaker imagines distant, powerful ocean waves relentlessly crashing against a shore.
* Troubled by legends of ghouls in bitter frost, the speaker confronts a unsettling fear of mortality and burial.

* Realizing that their youth has passed, the speaker feels overwhelmed by fear and loneliness, ultimately succumbing to tears in the silence.

outputs.L1:
Here are three polished versions of the text, tailored for different contexts (literary prose, formal prose, and refined verse), while keeping all original details, imagery, and meaning completely intact.

### Option 1: Elevated Literary Prose (Recommended)
> I awoke late into the cold night and listened to the wind. Lying in silence with my eyes closed, I realized how intangible words truly are, surrounded by the hollow darkness beneath my roof and the windowpanes rattling in the gale. 
> 
> As I lay there, I imagined distant, dark seas with towering waves crashing upon the sand, their receding tides echoing in eternal thunder. In those quiet moments, my thoughts turned to you, my friend, pondering what dark dealings ghouls might have—if such legends are true—in the low inland hollows of the earth, beneath the shadowed moon, amid the moaning night and bitter frost. I felt a sudden dread that the long-buried treasures of my mortal frame, surrendered to this earth, might fall into their hands. 
> 
> With neither companion nor ghost beside me, I felt deeply lonely, recalling distant gardens, the fragrance of lilacs, and late-summer twilights descending upon that familiar town. Lying there, I realized how my years had slipped away from me. I found myself absurdly frightened of the cold bed and the wind, left entirely alone with the silence and the quiet onset of tears.

---

### Option 2: Formal & Elegant Prose 
> Awakening late in the cold night, I lay silently with my eyes closed, listening to the wind and reflecting on the impermanence of words. The darkness beneath my roof felt empty as the wind battered the rattling windowpanes. 
> 
> In my mind, I pictured far-off black seas whose heavy waves plunge onto the shore, receding continuously in a perpetual thunder. Lying there, I pondered, my friend, whether legend holds true regarding the ghostly gatherings in the earth's low inland hollows—under the moon's shade, amid the frost and the night's mournful wind. I feared that the remains of my bones, long committed to this earth, might ultimately tumble into their hands. 
> 
> Completely alone, with neither lover nor spirit beside me, I remembered old gardens, the scent of lilacs, and the late summer twilights settling over that distant town. I recognized that my years had departed, and I was struck by an absurd dread of the cold bed and the wind—isolated in the silence, yielding to tears.

---

### Option 3: Polished Poetic Verse (Maintaining original form)
> Awaking late into the freezing night, I heard the wind,  
> And lay in silent darkness, eyes held shut,  
> Knowing how ghostlike and fleeting words remain—  
> Beneath this roof, an empty gloom,  
> As wind roughens the rattling windowpanes.  
> 
> I lay and imagined, somewhere far away,  
> Black, heavy-shouldered seas crashing on the sand,  
> Their ebbing currents thundering forever.  
> So lying, my friend, I wondered what dark trade  
> Ghouls hold—if the legends be true—  
> In low inland hollows beneath the moon's shadow,  
> Amid the night's moaning and the bitter frost;  
> And feared lest the riches of my long-buried bones  
> Should tumble at last into their hands.  
> 
> With no girl or ghost beside me in my loneliness,  
> I recalled past gardens, the scent of lilacs,  
> And summer twilight falling late upon that town.  
> I lay and felt my vanished years depart,  
> Fearing the cold bed and the restless wind—  
> Absurdly alone with silence and the trick of tears.
outputs.L2:
Roused from sleep during a freezing hour late at night, I listened to the gusts of air outside. I remained unmoving with eyelids drawn, reflecting on the incorporeal nature of speech, the vacant gloom beneath my roof, and my windowpanes shaking from the harsh gale. 

As I lay there, my mind pictured distant, massive dark waters crashing heavily onto sandy shores, their tide flowing backward amidst continuous, thunderous noise. In this position, I addressed a companion, pondering whether myth or truth describes the dealings of ghouls within deep, inland hollows shrouded by lunar shadows, while severe frost took hold and the night groaned. A dread overcame me that my own valuable bones—surrendered to the soil long ago—might fall into the possession of these creatures. 

Lacking any female partner or phantom beside me, I felt isolated and recalled cultivated plant grounds, the perfume of lilacs, and late summer dusk settling over a certain municipality. Remaining in bed, I recognized that my past years had vanished, leaving me unreasonably terrified of the frigid mattress and the howling wind, entirely alone with the quiet and the impulse to cry.
outputs.L3:
I awoke to a biting chill, finding myself entirely alone in the heavy darkness of the house. Outside, a furious wind battered the structure, making every windowpane rattle violently in its frame. The house felt vast and vacant, filled only with the unsettling rhythm of the storm and the freezing air that crept across the floorboards.

Unable to sleep, I lay paralyzed in the dark, my thoughts drifting far beyond the confines of the room. In the roaring of the wind, I began to imagine a distant, primordial coastline where monstrous ocean waves smashed relentlessly against the shore. I could almost hear the crushing weight of the water, an immense and uncaring power churning in the pitch-black night.

As the cold deepened, grim thoughts began to take hold. I was haunted by old tales of ghouls creeping through the bitter frost, folklore that now felt terrifyingly close. These unnatural horrors melted into a much deeper, more grounded existential dread: the terrifying reality of my own mortality. I was consumed by a sudden, overwhelming fear of death, picturing the absolute cold and solitude of being laid to rest beneath the earth.

Drowning in this isolation, I desperately tried to anchor my mind to something gentle. I sought refuge in the vault of my memory, calling forth the vivid warmth of past summers. I remembered the intoxicating fragrance of blooming gardens, the soft glow of golden twilights, and the comforting embrace of a gentle evening breeze. For a brief, fragile moment, these nostalgic visions offered a respite from the freezing night.

Yet, the illusion could not hold. A sudden, sharp realization pierced through the memories: those summer days were long gone, and my youth had vanished with them, never to return. The contrast between that lost warmth and my current cold reality was too much to bear. Overwhelmed by a crushing wave of loneliness and terror, I yielded to the weight of the dark, weeping silently into the cold night air.
outputs.L4:
The sudden break from sleep was not gentle; it was a violent yank into the frigid reality of the midnight hour. I lay rigid beneath the thin blankets, listening to the wind howl like a grieving beast through the skeletal branches of the oaks outside. The house groaned around me, a hollow, echoing shell. I was entirely alone. The cold air seeped through the hidden cracks in the window frame, settling on my skin like a shroud, carrying with it a sudden, suffocating panic that had no name, yet knew me intimately. 

Rising from the bed, the dull ache in my joints betrayed the quiet rebellion of my aging body. I pulled my robe tight and pressed my forehead against the icy glass of the bedroom window. Below, the garden was a wasteland of dark shadows and frost-bitten earth. The moon offered no warmth, casting only a pale, sickly glow over a landscape stripped of vitality. In that desolate vista, I saw my own inner landscape reflected back at me—barren, shivering, and stripped of bloom. The icy gale outside felt like a physical manifestation of my own approaching winter, a brutal reminder that time cares nothing for the fleeting warmth of a human life. The specter of mortality, once a distant shadow on the horizon, now stood firmly at the foot of my bed.

Desperate to escape the encroaching darkness, my mind sought refuge in the sanctuary of the past. I closed my eyes and reached back into the vault of memory. Suddenly, I was young again—bathed in the golden, endless light of late summer. I remembered the scent of sun-warmed pine, the reckless speed of my own legs as I ran through open fields, and the effortless, roaring rhythm of a heart that felt invincible. Time had once seemed like an ocean—boundless, eternal, and mine to conquer. In those vibrant days, death was a myth invented for the old, and solitude was merely a choice, never a sentence.

But the illusion could not hold against the persistent battering of the night wind. Opening my eyes, the golden warmth evaporated, leaving me stranded in the dark once more. A crushing realization hit me with the weight of an avalanche: those bright days were not merely behind me—they were irrevocably gone. The decades had slipped through my fingers like fine sand, unnoticed and uncaptured, until only a few grains remained. How had the years evaporated so silently? Where had the vibrant young man gone, and who was this frail stranger occupying his skin?

A heavy, unbidden grief welled up from deep within my chest, breaking over me in silent, painful sobs. It was not merely a sorrow for my lost youth, but a profound and visceral dread of what lay ahead. There was no one in the empty house to hold my hand, no gentle voice to whisper reassurances into the dark, no companion to share the burden of this final, terrifying truth. In the absolute stillness of the freezing room, punctuated only by the relentless storm outside, I confronted the ultimate, poignant horror of our existence: we may live among others, but to face the relentless march of time, and the looming darkness at its end, is a burden we must carry in absolute, terrifying solitude.
outputs.L5:
The world often feels loudest right before it settles down for the night. As the hours grow **late**, the frantic energy of the day begins to fade, replacing the ambient noise of daily routine with a deep, contemplative stillness. It is during **these** quiet hours that the mind finally finds the space to wander, reflect, **and** process everything that transpired before dawn breaks again.

In the constant rush of modern life, we rarely pause to appreciate the subtle shifts happening around us. Yet, when the evening settles **and** shadows lengthen across the room, time seems to stretch. **These** fleeting moments of solitude are essential for restoring our mental balance, offering a temporary sanctuary from the relentless pace of our obligations. 

Whether we spend this **late** hour reading, listening to gentle music, or simply sitting in quiet contemplation, it serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of slowing down. Embracing **these** peaceful intervals allows us to process the day that was **and** prepare to greet the coming morning with a renewed sense of clarity.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a melancholic poem about lying awake during a cold, windy night and contemplating loneliness and mortality.
counterfactuals.output:
The winter gale assaults the glass,
A shiver runs through floor and beam.
I watch the ghostly shadows pass,
Trapped in the space without a dream.

The bed is vast, the sheets are chill,
The room breathes out a frosty sigh.
The wind outside is fierce and shrill,
While in the heavy dark I lie.

It howls just like a grieving ghost,
And echoes in the empty space;
I am a pale, forgotten host,
Who leaves no shadow and no trace.

No lingering hand, no breathing soul,
To share the quiet in my chest.
The biting dark demands its toll,
And turns my sleeplessness to unrest.

I think of how the hours creep,
How flesh and bone are bound to rust,
How all we love is swept so deep
Into the cold and indifferent dust.

How brief the spark, how swift the end,
To burn awhile, then turn to clay—
The wind foretells what time will send,
And blows my fragile youth away.

So here I lie, and count my breath,
Beneath the ceiling’s weight of black,
Suspended between sleep and death,
With night ahead, and no way back.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem in a reflective, slightly archaic unrhymed verse style. The speaker should be lying awake in bed listening to a storm outside, shifting from thoughts of wild oceans to eerie fears of ghouls, before drifting into nostalgic memories of summer and feeling the weight of their aging body.
counterfactuals.output:
The timber groans beneath the tempest’s tread,
And I, encased within these woollen folds,
Lie mute and listening to the wildered dark.
The rain strikes furious measures on the glass,
A desperate knocking at my quiet room.

Methinks the storm hath torn the ocean loose
To fling her black, crest-foaming waters high;
Far off, upon the fathomless expanse,
Great hulks are tossed like straw upon the swell,
And sunken leviathans stir the silt
In cold, unlit abysses of the deep.

Yet deeper than the sea, a shadow crawls—
A fright of shapes that haunt the gale’s lament.
What ghouls are these that scrape the timbered eaves?
Thin, pale-limbed specters born of wind and night,
Unquiet things that whisper at the latch
And seek to chill the blood within my breast
With ancient, half-forgotten tales of dread.

I press mine eyelids shut to banish them,
And flee in thought to some forgotten noon,
When summer held the world in golden thrall.
I see again the clover-scented field,
The orchard heavy with the warmth of dusk,
Where once I ran, unburdened, swift, and young,
Beneath a sky untouched by cloud or storm,
And drank the liquid sunlight from the air.

Ah, but the sun is set, the field turned grey.
I feel the heavy vessel of my flesh,
The aching timber of these weary bones,
This slow and stiffening clay that binds me fast.
The tempest roars without, yet softly now,
As sleep arrives to weigh my spirit down,
And draw the blanket over age and night.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the experience of late-night insomnia in a cold house through verse, using vivid imagery of rattling windowpanes, distant crashing waves, and the sudden realization of how empty and quiet life has become.
counterfactuals.output:
Three a.m. blooms in shades of steel,
A frozen weight I cannot shake.
The dark is something I can feel,
And every nerve is pinned awake.
My breath plumes white in indoor air,
A pale ghost drifting through the room,
Where winter climbs the drafty stair
To settle in the quiet gloom.

Against its sash, the thin glass yields—
A sharp and frantic, shivering rattle,
As gales that swept the frozen fields
Renew their long, relentless battle.
And far beyond the headland’s steep,
A muffled, heavy thunder raves:
The dark, dark rhythm of the deep,
The churn of distant, crashing waves.

The radiator hums its dirge,
Then clicks and cools to icy stone.
The shadows on the wallpaper surge,
And leave me colder, more alone.
I wrap the blanket tight and turn,
Awaiting sleep that will not come,
While overhead the cold stars burn,
And all my aching limbs grow numb.

And then it hits me, sudden, stark—
A truth that cuts straight to the bone,
Unfolded in the hollow dark
Where I lie motionless, alone:
How vast the silence has become,
How empty every hallway stands,
How quiet life is, now that some
Great tide has washed away my plans.

No voices linger in the hall,
No echoes answer from the street;
Just dust motes rising, bound to fall,
And frost that creeps beneath my feet.
The sea still pounds the distant shore,
The window rattles in the gale,
And I am left, forevermore,
A stranger in a home grown pale.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you write an atmospheric, atmospheric-gothic poem about being alone at night, hearing the wind, and fearing for one's own mortality while remembering the scent of lilacs and lost youth?
counterfactuals.output:
The candle gutters in the drafty hall,
A drowning ember in a sea of shade;
The shadows lengthen on the peeling wall,
Where once the gold of morning light had played.

Outside, the midnight wind begins to scream,
It claws the windowpane with frozen bone,
And shakes the timber, shattering my dream,
To leave me trembling in the dark, alone.

It sings a dirge of rot, decay, and dust,
A hollow warning that my time is brief;
My beating heart feels heavy, struck with rust,
As fragile as a fallen, autumn leaf.

Yet through the terror of this black expanse,
A sudden ghost invades the heavy room:
The scent of lilacs, sweet as old romance,
Escaping from a long-forgotten bloom.

It breathes of youth, when all the world was young,
When sunlit hours were deep, and soft, and slow,
Before the bitter songs of age were sung,
Before I learned how cold the wind could blow.

Now trapped within a slow, expiring breath,
I mourn the youth I cannot catch again—
Smelling the past, while listening for Death,
Who waits outside my window in the rain.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Give me a sad, contemplative poem about getting old, being alone in bed on a freezing winter night, and crying over lost years.
counterfactuals.output:
The frost grows thick upon the pane,  
A silver lace of biting cold.  
I pull the heavy quilt up high,  
And feel the weight of being old.  

My breath hangs pale in frigid air,  
A fragile ghost, so thin and slow.  
The bed is vast, the shadows dark,  
Where no one sleeps, where no one goes.  

Where did the golden summers fly?  
The years I thought were mine to keep?  
They slipped like water through my hands,  
While I was careless, fast asleep.  

A tear runs warm against my cheek,  
Then turns to ice within the gloom.  
I weep for time I squandered so,  
Trapped in this cold and quiet room.  

For voices silenced by the decades,  
For open doors I walked on past,  
For all the love I held too loose,  
And days that vanished far too fast.  

The wall clock ticks its hollow measure,  
Indifferent to the fading light.  
I fold my aching, withered hands,  
And mourn my youth into the night.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
